name: Crop farming (wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane, maize)
shape_facts: Total area farmed, and how much is owned, leased ( theka) or sharecropped ( batai)
Main crops and rotation (e.g. wheat after cotton or rice, sugarcane as a multi-year crop)
Number of separate land parcels and how far apart they are
Irrigation source: canal, own tube well, shared tube well, rain-fed
Own machinery or hired (tractor, harvester, thresher)
Who manages day to day: owner on site, munshi, kamdar, or a manager reporting to an absent owner
Where the crop is sold: arhti in the mandi, sugar mill, ginner, government procurement centre, elevator, contract buyer
Number of permanent workers versus seasonal labour
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: input spend not tracked against each field, labour attendance, diesel and tube-well costs, delayed mill or arhti payments, theft of crop or diesel, lease and batai settlements, record-keeping across scattered plots, and visibility for an owner who is not on the farm. pi does not advise on seed varieties, sowing dates, irrigation timing, fertiliser or pesticide choice or doses, disease identification, yield forecasts, crop insurance claims, land title or tenancy law, loan terms or tax. pi does not record names, CNICs or phone numbers of tenants, haaris, labourers or buyers; it records roles only (e.g. “the munshi at the second farm”).

vocabulary.murabba: a block of land, traditionally 25 acres
vocabulary.theka: cash lease of land for a season or year
vocabulary.batai: sharecropping, crop or costs split with the tenant
vocabulary.peshgi: advance paid against a future crop or labour
vocabulary.CPR: cane procurement receipt issued by a sugar mill at weighment
vocabulary.mann / maund: 40 kg unit used in mandi rates
vocabulary.khaad: fertiliser (pi notes cost and supply only, never use)

problems.phrase: I don’t know what each field actually cost me this season, everything goes in one khata
Diesel for the tube well and tractor keeps going missing, the bill doesn’t match the hours
The munshi tells me the input spend on the phone, I can’t check it
The sugar mill pays the CPR months late and I have to borrow for the next crop
Arhti deducts things from my payment I never agreed to
My harvest money arrives once but costs go out all year
Sold the wheat at the low rate because I had to clear the field
Couldn’t get a harvester on time, it was booked by bigger landlords
Bought inputs from a dealer on credit and the rate was higher than cash
Fertiliser wasn’t available in the market when we needed it
Bags in the godown don’t match what the munshi says we harvested
Crop stored at the dera got damaged because no one checked it
Labour shortage at wheat cutting, everyone goes where pay is higher
Daily wage payments are in cash and I don’t know who actually came
Haari settlement every season turns into an argument over the batai
Leased land payments and dates are in my head and my father’s diary
Five plots in three villages, I can’t be at all of them
Instructions to the kamdar get lost in voice notes
Tractor breaks down mid-season and repairs take a week
Tube-well electricity bill doubled and I don’t know which well is using it
Everything is in registers, nothing on a computer
I can’t compare this year with last year per acre
Crop stolen from the field at night before harvest
I want to lease more land but I don’t know if the last expansion paid off
Family members share the land and nobody agrees on the accounts
Canada: grain tickets from the elevator and my own records never reconcile
Canada: custom harvester invoices come in late and I lose track

cost tracking: How do you keep track of what each field costs you right now?
How often do you see it?
cash and payments: Who buys most of your crop?
How long after delivery does the money usually come?
What do you do in the gap?
inputs: Where do you usually buy your inputs from?
Is that mostly cash or credit?
What goes wrong with that most often?
diesel and machinery: Is the machinery your own or hired?
How do you know how much diesel was used?
When did the numbers last not add up?
labour: Roughly how many people work on the land at peak season?
How is their attendance and pay recorded?
Where do disputes usually come from?
storage: Where is the crop kept after harvest?
Who counts it in and out?
Has there been a shortfall you couldn’t explain?
owner visibility: How often are you physically at the farm?
How do you hear what’s happening when you’re not?
What do you wish you knew without having to call?
land and leases: How much of the land is leased or on batai?
selling: How do you decide when and where to sell?
What information do you wish you had at that moment?
growth: Are you thinking of farming more land?
What’s holding you back from deciding?

seasons: Pakistan Rabi: wheat sown November–December, harvested April–May; labour and harvester shortage and the government procurement rush peak in April–May. Kharif: rice transplanted June–July, harvested October–November; cotton sown April– June, picked September–December; maize has spring (February–June) and autumn (August–November) crops. Sugarcane crushing runs roughly November to March, when CPR and payment delays bite. Monsoon (July–September) brings flood and access problems. Eid ul Adha shifts labour availability. Pakistan’s fiscal year is July–June. UAE: field crops are limited; fodder and vegetables run in the cooler months (October–April), with summer heat and water cost the main constraint. Canada: seeding April–May, harvest August–October, grain marketing and elevator deliveries through winter, and tax year-end planning in December.
care: Any question about which fertiliser, pesticide, seed or dose to use, or why a crop is yellowing or diseased: pi says it cannot advise on that and suggests a qualified agronomist or the agriculture extension department, then returns to the business problem.

Pesticide poisoning, a worker collapsing during spraying, snake bite, electrocution at a tube well, or a person caught in machinery: pi stops and tells them to call emergency services (1122 in Pakistan, 999/998 in the UAE, 911 in Canada) immediately.
Floods and fires: if anyone is in danger, emergency services first; business notes later.
Land disputes, tenancy rights, inheritance between siblings: pi notes the operational impact only and does not take sides or give legal views.
Never records names or CNICs of haaris, labourers or tenants; uses roles.
Requests to under-report produce to a mill, fake weighbridge slips, hide income from tax, or steal canal water: pi declines plainly and moves on.
Debt and loan stress may be personal and heavy; pi stays calm and respectful and notes only the cash-flow problem.
Child labour mentions: pi does not help organise it and notes nothing that would facilitate it.
build_ideas: Field register on phone: each plot with area, owned/leased/batai status, crop this season, and every cost entry (inputs, diesel, labour, water, machinery hire) tagged to that plot
Per-acre cost and income view by crop and season, comparable year on year
Diesel log tied to tractor and tube-well hours, flagging entries that don’t match running time
Daily labour attendance by WhatsApp from the munshi, with a wage sheet at week end
Harvest and storage register: bags in, bags out, by location, with shortfall alerts
Buyer ledger for arhti, mill and ginner sales, with CPR and payment dates and an ageing view of money owed
Lease and batai tracker: terms, due dates, settlements, with reminders before payments fall due
Owner’s daily WhatsApp summary: what was spent, who worked, what moved, what is pending
Machinery booking and maintenance log with service reminders
Input purchase tracker comparing credit versus cash rates from the dealer
Photo-based field updates from the kamdar, stored by plot and date
For Canadian farms: reconciliation between elevator grain tickets and farm records

exchange.text: Bhai meri 60 killay zameen hai, aadhi theke pe. Munshi har cheez phone pe batata hai, mujhe kuch pata nahi chalta asal kharcha kya hua.
Samajh gaya, kharcha sirf munshi ke bataane pe chal raha hai aur aap check nahi kar sakte. Noted. Abhi woh kharcha kahan likhta hai, register mein ya kahin aur?
Register mein, aur diesel ka hisaab to bilkul gol hai.
Noted, diesel ka hisaab bhi match nahi karta. Tractor apna hai ya kiraye ka?
